variation_strategy: Five features hit different layers: cross-parameter validation (core.py Option/Command.parse_args), a type's matching semantics (Choice), interactive input retry policy (termui.prompt), help-layout output (HelpFormatter), and filesystem type validation (Path). Each has its own interacting rule set (explicit-source eligibility, exact-vs-prefix precedence, attempt counting across error kinds, numbering/indent/width, suffix versus existence/dash/bytes).

features.title: Option conflicts_with and requires declarations
features.problem: Click has no declarative way to say two options are mutually exclusive or that one option needs another. Users hand-write callbacks that cannot tell explicit values from defaults.
behavior: conflicts_with and requires are sequences of parameter NAMES (the python names, as in ctx.params). Stored as tuples on the Option.
A parameter counts as 'explicit' if ctx.get_parameter_source(name) is ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT or PROMPT. DEFAULT_MAP, DEFAULT and no source are not explicit.
Checks run in Command.parse_args after every parameter has been processed (before leftover-args check). Params are examined in the order of command.get_params(ctx).

For each explicit option A and each name B in A.conflicts_with: if B is explicit, ctx.fail("Option 'A' cannot be used together with option 'B'.") where A is A.name and B is the listed name, each in single quotes, e.g. "Option 'json_' cannot be used together with option 'csv'." The first violation found raises.
For each explicit option A and each name B in A.requires: if B is not explicit, ctx.fail("Option 'A' requires option 'B'."). conflicts_with checks for an option are done before its requires checks.
Conflicts are symmetric: declaring conflicts_with on only one of the two options is enough to trigger the error.
Failure is a UsageError (exit code 2) raised through ctx.fail.
interaction_rules: Only explicit sources count: an option that conflicts but whose value came from default or default_map does not trigger an error, and a required-by option satisfied only by default still counts as missing.
When option A both conflicts with C and requires B and both are violated, the conflict error is reported first.
Under ctx.resilient_parsing (shell completion) no validation is performed.
Names that match no parameter on the command are treated as non-explicit (so requires fails, conflicts never fires).
edge_cases_and_errors: conflicts_with='json' (a bare str) raises TypeError("'conflicts_with' must be a sequence of names, not a string.") at Option construction; same for requires with "'requires' ...".
A name appearing in its own conflicts_with raises TypeError("Option 'x' cannot conflict with itself.").
Flag options with value False given explicitly (--no-x) are still explicit.
Empty sequences (default) disable the feature entirely.
backward_compatibility: Options without these kwargs behave identically; parse_args does no extra work visible to users.
Option.to_info_dict is unchanged (does not include the new keys).

examples.expected: exit_code 2; stderr contains "Error: Option 'json_' cannot be used together with option 'csv'."
exit_code 0 because a came from DEFAULT

acceptance_criteria: Two conflicting explicit options exit 2 with the exact conflict message.
requires missing option fails with exact message; supplying it via environment variable satisfies it.
Defaults do not count as explicit.
Bare string argument raises TypeError with exact message.
Conflict reported before requires failure; no validation when resilient_parsing.
features.extension_point: Option.__init__ stores the attributes; Command.parse_args runs checks after the handle_parse_result loop.
features.novelty_rationale: The report lists cross-parameter validation as a gap; nothing in the repo or upstream-do-not-propose list covers it.
features.difficulty_rationale: Eligibility depends on parameter sources, ordering of checks, and name vs. declaration-string confusion (python name, not flag).

features.title: Choice allow_prefix unambiguous abbreviation
features.problem: Choice requires full values. CLIs often want 'pro' to resolve to 'production' when unambiguous.
behavior: With allow_prefix=True, convert first tries the existing exact match (using normalize_choice, honoring case_sensitive and token_normalize_func); an exact match always wins.
If no exact match, the normalized input is compared with str.startswith against each normalized choice. Exactly one match returns the ORIGINAL choice object (e.g. the Enum member or int).
Zero matches fail with the existing get_invalid_choice_message.

Two or more matches fail with BadParameter message "{value!r} is ambiguous; it could be one of {matches}." where value is the raw input and matches is ', '.join(repr(m)) of the normalized matching choices in declaration order, e.g. "'pr' is ambiguous; it could be one of 'prod', 'prof'."
An empty string never prefix-matches (it is only valid if an exact normalized '' choice exists).
shell_complete is unchanged.
interaction_rules: Exact match beats prefix: choices ['pro','prod'] with value 'pro' returns 'pro'.
With case_sensitive=False, prefix comparison uses the casefolded normalized forms, so 'PR' matches 'production'.
Duplicate normalized choices that match the prefix are deduplicated by normalized value (preserving order) before the ambiguity decision.
edge_cases_and_errors: allow_prefix=True with a single choice: prefix still resolves, invalid values still use singular invalid-choice message.
Value that is not str (e.g. int 1 with choices [10, 11]) is normalized via str() so '1' prefix matches 10 and 11 -> ambiguous.
allow_prefix non-bool is not validated.
ctx=None is tolerated.
backward_compatibility: Default allow_prefix=False leaves all conversion identical.
to_info_dict output of Choice is unchanged by default; tests/test_info_dict stays valid.

examples.expected: BadParameter: "'pr' is ambiguous; it could be one of 'prod', 'prof'."

acceptance_criteria: Unique prefix returns original choice.
Ambiguous prefix raises BadParameter with exact message.
Exact match wins over longer prefix match.
Case-insensitive prefix works and returns original casing.
Default behaviour rejects prefixes with the old message.
features.extension_point: Choice.__init__ and Choice.convert fallback after exact-match failure.
features.novelty_rationale: Choice has no abbreviation support; NoSuchCommand suggestions are different and listed upstream.
features.difficulty_rationale: Precedence of exact vs. prefix, normalization and case folding, and returning original objects.

features.title: prompt max_attempts retry limit
features.problem: click.prompt loops forever on invalid input, which hangs scripted sessions.
public_interface: click.prompt(text, ..., show_choices=True, max_attempts: int | None = None)
behavior: max_attempts=None keeps infinite retry.
An 'attempt' is one full pass of the outer loop that fails: a UsageError from value_proc, or a confirmation mismatch. Empty input with default=None (inner loop re-ask) does not count.
After the Nth failed attempt (N=max_attempts) the usual 'Error: ...' message is echoed and then Abort is raised instead of reprompting.
A successful attempt returns normally even on the last allowed try.
Error message echoing for the failing attempts is unchanged (including hide_input masking).
interaction_rules: Failed attempts from value_proc errors and from confirmation mismatch share one counter.
The default value is also run through value_proc; if it fails it counts as an attempt.
edge_cases_and_errors: max_attempts=0 or negative raises ValueError('max_attempts must be at least 1.') before any prompting.
max_attempts=1 with a valid first answer returns it.
Non-int values such as 1.5 are not specified.
With confirmation_prompt and max_attempts=1, a mismatch echoes 'Error: The two entered values do not match.' then raises Abort.
backward_compatibility: All existing calls behave identically with max_attempts omitted.
Positional argument order of existing parameters unchanged (new kwarg last).

examples.expected: outputs "Error: 'x' is not a valid integer." twice then raises Abort
ValueError: max_attempts must be at least 1.

acceptance_criteria: Abort after N failures.
Success on last attempt returns value.
ValueError for <1 with exact message and no input read.
Mismatches count toward the limit.
Default behavior unchanged.
features.extension_point: Outer while loop in prompt around value_proc and confirmation comparison (termui.py ~260-286).
features.novelty_rationale: Report names a missing retry limit as a gap; not in upstream lists (PromptBuilder is formatting only).
features.difficulty_rationale: Which events count as attempts, ordering of echo versus Abort, and validation before I/O.

features.title: HelpFormatter.write_list bulleted and numbered lists
features.problem: Help text lists need hanging indents; only the \b marker preserves layout and does not wrap.
public_interface: HelpFormatter.write_list(self, items: Iterable[str], bullet: str | None = '*', start: int | None = None) -> None
behavior: Each item is written as one wrapped block with a hanging indent; the marker is followed by one space.
Marker for bullet style is `bullet`; if start is not None, items are numbered 'start.', 'start+1.', ... and bullet is ignored.
The marker starts at self.current_indent spaces; continuation lines are indented to current_indent + len(marker) + 1.
Wrapping uses wrap_text(item, self.width, initial_indent=marker_prefix, subsequent_indent=hanging) so width counts the full line; each item ends with '\n'.
Numbered markers are right-aligned to the widest marker in the list so text columns align, e.g. ' 9.' and '10.'.
An empty items iterable writes nothing.
interaction_rules: Respects indent()/dedent() and section(): inside a section the list is indented by indent_increment.
bullet=None with start=None writes items with no marker and hanging indent of current_indent only (plain indented blocks).
edge_cases_and_errors: start negative raises ValueError('start must be non-negative.').
Empty bullet string '' behaves like bullet=None.
An empty item string writes just the marker (rstripped) and newline.
Non-str items raise whatever wrap_text raises (not specified).
backward_compatibility: No existing method changes; write_dl/write_text output unchanged.
HelpFormatter subclasses overriding write still intercept the output since write_list uses self.write.

examples.code:
f=click.HelpFormatter(width=20); f.write_list(['one','two words here and more'])
f.getvalue()
examples.expected:
'* one
* two words here and
  more
'

examples.code: f=click.HelpFormatter(width=40); f.write_list(['a']*10, start=1) ; first two lines

acceptance_criteria: Bullet wrapping hanging indent exact.
Numbered alignment for 9->10 crossing.
Indent respected.
Empty list writes nothing.
Negative start raises ValueError.
features.novelty_rationale: Hanging-indent list helpers are listed as a gap in formatting.py and absent from the repo.
features.difficulty_rationale: Alignment arithmetic, hanging indent widths and interaction with current_indent.

features.title: Path suffixes check
features.problem: click.Path cannot restrict file extensions, so users validate in callbacks.
public_interface: click.Path.__init__(..., executable=False, suffixes: Sequence[str] | None = None)
behavior: suffixes is a sequence of extensions including the dot, e.g. ('.txt','.md'). Stored lower-cased as a tuple, or None.

In convert, after the dash short-circuit, the final path component of the ORIGINAL value (os.fsdecode, os.path.basename) lower-cased must end with one of the suffixes; compare via str.endswith, so '.tar.gz' works as a multi-dot suffix.
Failure: self.fail("{name} {filename!r} must end with one of: .txt, .md.") using name.title() and format_filename(value) like other messages, suffixes joined by ', '.
The suffix check runs before os.stat, so it applies even when exists=False and the file does not exist.
Directories are also subject to the check (a directory without a matching suffix fails).
interaction_rules: allow_dash with value '-' skips the suffix check like all other checks.
The suffix check precedes exists/file/dir checks: a missing file with a bad suffix and exists=True reports the suffix error.
Matching is case-insensitive on the value ('A.TXT' passes for '.txt').
bytes values are decoded with os.fsdecode for the check.
edge_cases_and_errors: suffixes given as a bare str raises TypeError("'suffixes' must be a sequence of strings, not a string.").
A suffix not starting with '.' raises ValueError("Suffix 'txt' must start with a dot.").
Empty sequence is treated as None (no check).
Basename without extension e.g. 'Makefile' fails.

examples.expected: BadParameter: "Path 'a.py' must end with one of: .txt, .md." (name is 'File' if dir_okay=False)

acceptance_criteria: Allowed suffix case-insensitive passes.
Rejected suffix raises with exact message.
Suffix error precedes exists error.
Dash skips check with allow_dash.
Bare str and missing dot raise exact errors.
features.extension_point: Path.__init__ and start of the non-dash branch in Path.convert (types.py ~1172).
features.novelty_rationale: The report lists extension checks as a Path gap; not present upstream.
features.difficulty_rationale: Check ordering relative to stat and dash, case folding, multi-dot suffixes, and constructor validation.
